scenarios.name: fit-parts-order: a plain box (no unsupported overhang) gets outer wall/inner wall as a per-object override
fit-parts-order: a mushroom (unsupported overhang area > 0) keeps the project order
top Z at the factory default (below the creators' range) is only a suggestion
top Z above the creators' range is applied (relato), bottom Z follows
top Z at the top end of the range (0.28 at 0.20 mm = ratio 1.4) selects neither branch
a1 tall narrow part with the preset auto_brim: Outer brim only is a suggestion
ABS on the X2D: a wider outer_and_inner brim is not downgraded to outer_only
X2D with three colours on one nozzle gets the prime tower
By object with timelapse Smooth: Smooth is removed and no tower is added
ironing on a 0.12 mm Fine preset (5 layers, 0.6 mm): the top shell minimum (hipotese, suggestion) fires on the thickness alone
generic PETG body with a cubic infill keeps its pattern (petg-infill-gyroid absent from the applied PETG actions)
PLA body with a PETG interface is not slowed to 60 mm/s for gloss
alternate extra wall with ensure_vertical_shell_thickness none is not turned on
alternate extra wall with the factory vertical shell gets Partial
silk retraction speed is not written on the X2D (scalar would raise the Bowden elements)
tall thin figurine on the A1 (PLA Basic, tree support in the G-code): every A1 tall-narrow rule is a hypothesis, so brim, acceleration, travel and tree style are only suggested and nothing is applied
scenarios.review: OK 10.2 (L391) and 6.3 (L215): brim 5-10 mm, travel < 400 mm/s, acceleration < 3000 mm/s2 and Strong/Hybrid are [relato]/[hipotese] tests, so suggestion-only matches their confidence; Top Z and critical-regions suggestions come from 6.2/6.3. DATA (policy): for the part the user names as most at risk nothing is applied; no measured trigger exists for tipping or adhesion, so a brim for a tall thin part is never automatic.

scenarios.name: tall thin figurine on the X2D: the tall-narrow rules are A1-only (moving bed), so nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK by silence: 10.2 describes the A1's moving bed (L389-391); the guide says nothing about tall parts on the X2D, so no action is the faithful result. DATA: silence is not evidence that the X2D is safe.

scenarios.name: tall thin figurine on the A1 with a fixed-width brim of 3 mm: the brim width choice (5 mm) is also only a suggestion
scenarios.review: OK 10.2 (L391): brim 5 to 10 mm [hipotese]; the width choice (5) is only a suggestion and the brim type, already outer_only, is untouched.

scenarios.name: large flat ABS plate on the X2D (brim needed): outer brim only and no cooling in the first 3 layers are applied; exhaust off and Shrinkage are suggestions
scenarios.review: OK 9.4 (L377): Outer brim only 5-8 mm with gap 0-0.1 mm and 3-4 no-cooling layers are [relato] (applied); exhaust 0% is marked [hipotese] there and Shrinkage 99.3-99.5% is [hipotese] (8.5 L325): suggestions. Width 5 and gap 0.1 are already inside the guide range and stay. DATA: 'large' is the declared flag object.is_large_part (the guide gives no threshold) and nothing in the slice measures warping (kb facts gcode.first_layer_contact_share / first_layer_brim_present exist, no action reads them), so the result is predictive and the report must say it was not verified by slicing.

scenarios.name: large flat ABS plate on the X2D whose project has the brim off (no_brim, width 0): outer brim only with 5 mm is applied
scenarios.review: OK 9.4 (L377): no_brim becomes outer_only with 5 mm, the low end of 5-8 mm; same predictive caveat as the previous case.

scenarios.name: small ABS part on the X2D (brim NOT needed): no brim rule fires, the project's brim settings stay; only the cooling and the two suggestions apply
scenarios.review: DATA: the guide ties the brim sentence to 'pecas grandes' (heat soak context, L377) but never says a small ABS part is safe without a brim; the data reads it as large-only. The no-brim result follows the data's reading, not an explicit guide statement. The 3-layer cooling delay applies to any ABS part (the guide does not restrict it).

scenarios.name: ABS on the X2D without a Studio version: every ABS rule needs Studio >= 2.8, the version is unknown, so every ABS rule is skipped as unknown and nothing is applied
scenarios.review: OK: applies_to >= 2.8 on every ABS action; an unknown version is unknown, not false (three-valued), so the rules are skipped as unknown and the project is left alone.

scenarios.name: large flat PLA plate on the X2D (no overhangs): the auxiliary-fan reduction to 20% is only a suggestion (hypothesis)
scenarios.review: OK 9.2 (L356): 0 to 20% auxiliary fan on boxes and large plates, keep it on small parts and parts with overhangs [hipotese]; 20% is the least intrusive end of the range, suggestion only. DATA: 'large' is a declared flag and nothing measures the corner lifting.

scenarios.name: small PLA part on the X2D: the guide keeps the auxiliary fan on small parts, so nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK 9.2 (L356): 'mantendo em pecas pequenas'.

scenarios.name: large PLA box with overhangs on the X2D: the guide keeps the auxiliary fan on parts with overhangs, so nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK 9.2 (L356): 'mantendo ... em pecas com balancos'.

scenarios.name: functional bracket on the A1 with 45-degree overhangs and four holes: all strength points are hypotheses (suggested), 45 degrees is above the 30-degree threshold so no support is needed, nothing is applied
scenarios.review: OK 8.3 (L309-314) and 8.5 (L324): functional 3-4 walls, 20-25%, Gyroid/Cubic/3D Honeycomb, top 5-6 layers / 1.0-1.2 mm, bottom 4-5 layers / 0.8-1.0 mm and hole compensation +0.05 to +0.15 mm are all [hipotese]; 45 degrees is above the 30-degree support threshold (6.1 L193) so mesh.unsupported_overhang_area_mm2 = 0 and no support is wanted, PROVIDED the threshold is a slope angle from the horizontal (the usual Studio meaning, assumed by the fact definition; the guide does not state the convention, rule bambu.support.overhang-without-support is nao verificado). DATA: the engine applies none of it, so a functional part is sliced with the project's own strength settings; the guide offers no measurable trigger for strength (policy 2 outcome), which is the opposite of 'the engine chooses inside the ranges'. The hole compensation is object scope and appears only as a suggestion.

scenarios.name: high-load bracket on the A1 that already has four walls: width, bonding temperature, extra wall and density rules are all hypotheses (suggested)
scenarios.review: OK 8.3-8.4 (L309-320): 4-6 walls, 25-30%, alternate extra wall + Partial, widths 0.55-0.6 mm, +5 to +10 C are all [hipotese]. DATA: the guide pairs the temperature rise with a 20-30% fan reduction (L320); only the temperature half is modelled, so +5 C alone is a partial application.

scenarios.name: functional part with no declared load class and no hole facts (facts missing): nothing is applied, nothing is suggested
scenarios.review: OK: with unknown facts every conditional rule is skipped as unknown; nothing is guessed.

scenarios.name: part with a long bridge, project with support off, before the first slice: the support ladder is post-slice, so nothing changes in round 0
scenarios.review: DATA: the guide has no bridge guidance at all (no bridge speed, flow or cooling advice; 'ponte' appears only for the purge tower, L227). Round 0 cannot react to a bridge because the only overhang rule is a post-slice ladder.

scenarios.name: part with a long bridge, first slice measured 0 support lines while the mesh has 420 mm2 of unsupported overhang: the support ladder takes its first step (enable_support 1)
scenarios.review: DATA: 6.5 (L233) says to look for overhangs without support, so checking is right, but mesh.unsupported_overhang_area_mm2 > 0 cannot tell a flat bridge from a sloped overhang (the guide gives no bridge criterion at all), so a bridge of any length turns tree(auto) support on. Confidence nao verificado (angle convention and area floor are not in the source); applied only because it is a measured ladder.

scenarios.name: part with a long bridge but hand-painted support in the 3MF: the ladder stays idle
scenarios.review: OK: painted support is the user's own placement (16, L590 Support painting) and the source rule's when_text says it is not considered; the ladder is idle when the 3MF already has painted support.

scenarios.name: organic miniature on the A1 (tiny, slender protrusions, tree support already in the G-code): first layer slowed to 25 mm/s, organic tree with one support wall and 3 interface layers applied; travel threshold, critical-only and the support distance are suggestions
scenarios.review: OK 10.4 (L399, first layer 15-25 mm/s [relato], 25 is the mildest), 6.3 (L215, Slim/Organic with 1 support wall [relato]) and 6.2 (L210, 3 interface layers); Top/Bottom Z below the range and the 0.5 mm travel threshold are [hipotese] suggestions. DATA: the same 10.4 sentence also lists brim and +5 C for tiny parts and neither is modelled, so a tiny miniature gets no brim; and tree_organic is the Studio default (L215 'O padrao e organic'), so that write is probably a no-op in Studio.

scenarios.name: generic (third-party) PETG on the A1 with a 230 C profile: the creators' PETG table is applied (temperature, flow, fans, volumetric cap, Normal Lift, Gyroid, 60 mm/s walls)
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L362-372): nozzle 250-265, flow 0.93-0.95, volumetric 9-13, fan min 15-20 / max 35-40 / overhang <= 80, off in the first 3 layers, Normal Lift 0.4, Gyroid, retraction 0.4-1.4 with wipe 2 mm (unchanged: already inside). DATA: tune.quality.outer-wall-gloss-speed (60 mm/s) and the 2500 mm/s2 cap (7.7 L292, [relato] about gloss) apply to every PETG or Silk part with the outer wall above 120 mm/s, functional or not: a time cost that only matters when surface gloss does.

scenarios.name: Bambu PETG Basic on the A1 with the preset values: the third-party PETG rules do not fire (profile name contains Bambu), nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L352, L364): 'para filamento Bambu o preset ja esta proximo'; the third-party rules are gated by the profile name (no Bambu), and a slowed outer wall keeps the gloss rule out.

scenarios.name: generic PETG on the X2D: the auxiliary fan goes to 0 and the fan/flow rules apply; the A1-only retraction rules do not fire
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L369, L348): auxiliary fan 0 for PETG, fan/flow table. The retraction rules are A1/A1 mini only because the X2D vector mixes direct drive and Bowden (5.2 L138-141). DATA: retraction length/speed and wipe of a third-party PETG on the X2D are not tuned (A1-only); Z-hop height and type are (unchanged here).

scenarios.name: generic PETG on the A1 where the user already holds every recommended value: nothing is applied and the value-less rules are reported as already satisfied
scenarios.review: OK: already-satisfied rules are reported as unchanged_already instead of being rewritten (fan off layers, volumetric cap, wipe/retraction speed, Z-hop height and type).

scenarios.name: PETG with the profile name unknown (fact missing): only the rule that does not need the profile fires (fan cap 50%); the third-party rules stay unknown
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L369, L372): a fan above 50-60% reduces layer adhesion, valid whatever the profile; the profile-dependent rules stay unknown.

scenarios.name: conflict on fan_max_speed: generic PETG with the fan at 100% matches both the 40% choice (priority 40) and the 50% cap (priority 39); the higher priority wins
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L369): creators' max 35-40% against 'acima de 50 a 60% reduz a adesao' (L372); the stricter 40 wins by priority and also satisfies the 50 cap.

scenarios.name: conflict on outer_wall_speed: a PETG QR plate at 200 mm/s matches the gloss choice (60, priority 40) and the QR choice (80, priority 39); 60 wins and lies inside the QR range 60 to 80
scenarios.review: OK 14.2 (L504, QR squares 60-80 mm/s) and 7.7 (L292, 60-120): 60 satisfies both ranges.

scenarios.name: conflict on outer_wall_speed with Silk: the 60 mm/s gloss choice (relato, priority 40) beats the ~50 mm/s anti-jam cap (hypothesis, priority 26)
scenarios.review: OK with caveat: 9.2 (L358) ~50 mm/s is an anti-jam test [hipotese], 7.7 (L292) 60-120 is gloss [relato]; they answer different problems and 60 is inside the creators' range. Silk volumetric 11 and retraction 25 stay suggestions.

scenarios.name: H2D project re-targeted to the X2D (fixture as is): the A1-only elephant-foot rule does not fire, the H2D 0.15 mm stays; Auto Lift becomes Spiral Lift (applied); the X2D first-layer flow and infill overlap are suggestions
scenarios.review: OK: the elephant-foot rule is gated by an A1 source (7.2 L258: X2D preset 0.15 equals the H2D value anyway); Auto Lift becomes Spiral Lift (5.2 L140, X2D filaments write Spiral); the first-layer flow 1.04 and infill overlap 50% are the [relato] workaround of L469 for the open gap bug. DATA: the guide has nothing on H2D to X2D beyond 'revise tudo' (3.3 L74); the engine does not rebuild the 5-variant H2D vectors into the 6-variant X2D ones.

scenarios.name: H2D project re-targeted to the X2D, auxiliary nozzle measured at 250 mm/s and 4000 mm/s2: the project still carries the five H2D direct-drive variants, so no element is a Bowden element and the caps cannot be written
scenarios.review: DATA/ENGINE: the G-code measures 250 mm/s and 4000 mm/s2 on the auxiliary nozzle (limit 200/1000, guide L49, L405, L451 [oficial]) but the project has no Bowden element, so the caps cannot be written and are reported as unchanged_already, i.e. 'satisfied'. A cap that cannot be written must surface as unresolved, never as already satisfied.

scenarios.name: A1 project re-targeted to the X2D: the elephant foot goes from the A1 preset 0.075 mm to the X2D preset 0.15 mm (preset, applied)
scenarios.review: OK 7.2 (L258) and 8.5 (L330): 0.075 mm (A1 preset) becomes 0.15 mm (X2D preset) [preset].

scenarios.name: A1 project re-targeted to the X2D whose elephant foot the user already tuned to 0.1 mm: not touched
scenarios.review: OK: a user value is not touched (L656 lists elephant foot by goal as an open divergence).

scenarios.name: user disabled Z-hop (z_hop 0) on an 80 mm part: Z-hop 0.4 is switched back on (travel without hop drags the nozzle over printed lines)
scenarios.review: OK 5.4 (L163): Z-hop on is mitigation 1 [relato]; 0.4 mm is the preset (5.2 L137).

scenarios.name: user disabled Z-hop on a 256 mm tall part: height plus 0.4 mm would leave the 256 mm Z range, so Z-hop is NOT switched on
scenarios.review: OK 12 (L455) and 18 (L639): height + Z-hop above 256 mm leaves the Z range. DATA: nothing else is offered (no reduced hop, no warning), so the part keeps its travel risk silently; the report must say travel protection is off for this part.

scenarios.name: filament override sets Z-hop to 0 while the machine has 0.4 mm: the filament Z-hop is raised to 0.4
scenarios.review: OK 3.1 (L60) and 17.1 (L603): the filament override beats the machine value. Risk noted by the data: a 0 may be deliberate.

scenarios.name: retraction set to 0 with Z-hop on (A1): the hop needs a retraction, so 0.8 mm is restored
scenarios.review: OK 5.1 (L131): no retraction, no hop.

scenarios.name: Z-hop type left on Auto Lift without a filament override (PLA): an explicit Spiral Lift is chosen
scenarios.review: OK 5.4 (L163) and 5.3 (L152, Auto rule 'nao verificado'): explicit type; Spiral because the manufacturer uses it on the X2D filaments (L154).

scenarios.name: Z-hop type left on Auto Lift with generic PETG: Normal Lift is chosen (creators' table) and the generic explicit-type rule stays out
scenarios.review: OK 9.3 (L370): PETG Z-hop Normal, 0.4 mm [relato]; Spiral may scrape PETG [hipotese] (5.3 L151).

scenarios.name: Z-hop type left on Auto Lift with Bambu PETG Basic: no rule acts (the manufacturer uses Spiral Lift for PETG and the guide records the Normal-versus-Spiral divergence), the type stays Auto Lift
scenarios.review: DATA: Auto Lift stays; the guide lists Normal versus Spiral for PETG as an open divergence (L656) and asks for an explicit type (L163), the data leaves Bambu PETG on Auto without telling the user.

scenarios.name: measured crossing travels (count 6) on A1 PLA Basic in Auto mode with Grid, first measured round: the travel ladder takes step 1, reduce_infill_retraction_mode Disabled (applied); the pattern stays Grid until a later round
scenarios.review: OK 5.4 (L162-164, L168), 5.5 (L176-179) and 18 (L633): the G-code read is what detects the bug; PLA/ABS Bambu have stickiness None, so Auto skips the infill retraction and Disabled always retracts [relato]; one ladder step per round, so Gyroid (5.6 L183, 'testes, nao garantias') waits for the next measured round. DATA: the trigger is any crossing (L633 gives no tolerance), so a single crossing travel is enough to change a project setting.

scenarios.name: same crossing travels on Bambu PETG in Auto mode (stickiness High) with Grid: Auto already retracts in infill for PETG, so step 1 is skipped by its guard (no 'Auto->Disabled' that does nothing) and the first measured round already takes step 2, Gyroid
scenarios.review: OK 5.5 (L176-179): Auto already retracts in infill for stickiness Medium/High (Bambu PETG is High), so Disabled would equal what was there; the step guard only_if (mode different from Auto, or some filament with stickiness None/Low) is false and the step is skipped without spending a slice round or listing a change that does nothing. Step 2 (Gyroid, 5.6 L183) is taken because the project uses Grid. DATA: the guard reads the stickiness LIST of the project (one entry per filament slot); in a mixed project one None/Low slot is enough to keep step 1, which may then be useless for the filament that crosses (the next slice measures it).

scenarios.name: unprotected travels measured (40) but none crosses printed extrusion: the travel ladder stays idle and nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK 5.4 (L168) and 18 (L633): the guide asks to read the G-code for travel without retraction or lift after extrusion; unprotected travels that cross nothing printed are reported (gcode.unprotected_travel_count) but are not what scrapes lines, so no setting is touched. DATA: the guide does not say the non-crossing ones are harmless; the severity it names is crossing a perimeter, support or top.

scenarios.name: crossing count not measured (G-code scan failed): the travel ladder trigger is unknown and nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK: an unknown trigger never moves a ladder and never counts as clean (analyzer-spec 1); the round reports the trigger as unknown with the missing fact.

scenarios.name: X2D, auxiliary nozzle measured at exactly 200 mm/s and 1000 mm/s2: the limit is not exceeded, so no cap is written
scenarios.review: OK L49, L405: the limit is 'no maximo' 200 mm/s and 1000 mm/s2, so exactly the limit is allowed.

scenarios.name: X2D, auxiliary nozzle measured at 250 mm/s and 4000 mm/s2: the 200 mm/s and 1000 mm/s2 caps are written on the Bowden elements only (official limit)
scenarios.review: OK L405, L451 [oficial]: caps 200 mm/s and 1000 mm/s2 on the Bowden elements only (the direct-drive elements keep 300 mm/s and 10000 mm/s2, L405).

scenarios.name: supports on ABS at 0.20 mm with Top Z 0.30 (above the 0.24 to 0.26 range): Top Z and Bottom Z are pulled to 0.24 (relato, applied)
scenarios.review: OK 6.2 (L203): ABS/ASA Top Z 0.24 to 0.26 [relato], start 0.24; Bottom Z follows the Top Z (L208).

scenarios.name: supports on PLA Silk at 0.20 mm with the factory Top Z 0.20: the guide's 0.26 to 0.28 is only a suggestion (hypothesis), nothing is applied
scenarios.review: OK 6.2 (L203): Silk/PETG 0.26-0.28 [relato], but the factory 1.0x against 1.2-1.4x is on the open-divergence list (L656), so the data keeps it a suggestion; the Silk row wins over the PLA row (priority).

scenarios.name: supports on PLA at 0.24 mm (no table row): the 1.2x to 1.4x formula branch below the range is a suggestion only
scenarios.review: OK 6.2 (L197): creators converge on 1.2-1.4x the layer height [relato]; there is no table row for 0.24, so the formula branch applies and, below the range, only suggests.

scenarios.name: supports with interface (120 lines) on PLA at 0.20 mm and Top Z 0.24: interface layers go to 3 and the interface spacing to 0.30 (relato, applied)
scenarios.review: OK 6.2 (L210-211): interface layers 3 and spacing 0.2-0.3 with Top Z calibrated (here 0.24 = 1.2x) [relato].

scenarios.name: A1 with three colours and the prime tower off: the tower is switched on (a purge tower is needed for the colour changes)
scenarios.review: OK 2 (L51): the A1 tower is 'necessaria em multicor' (the row has no confidence label; the data treats it as relato).

scenarios.name: A1 with three colours, tower already on and flush multiplier 1.0: the official starting point 0.9 is applied; the floor rule stays out
scenarios.review: OK 4.3 (L104): 0.8-0.9 is the manufacturer's starting point [oficial]. DATA: the guide itself calls it an indirect reading (L104, limit 3 L662) and says colour mixing must be validated per colour pair, yet 'oficial' makes it automatic and the engine cannot measure colour.

scenarios.name: multicolour face-down plate on the A1 (2 filaments, Textured PEI): the prime tower is switched on (applied); elephant foot 0, first layer 30 mm/s and bed +5 C are only suggestions (hypotheses)
scenarios.review: OK 14.6 (L541-543) and 8.5 (L331): elephant foot 0, first layer 30-35 mm/s, bed +5 C are [hipotese], so suggestions; the A1 tower applies because there are two colours (L51).

scenarios.name: keychain with Topmost-surface ironing and two top levels: Top surfaces, flow 20%, speed 50 mm/s and top surface speed 100 mm/s are applied; denser infill is a suggestion
scenarios.review: OK 14.1-14.2 (L485-499): Top surfaces for two levels, speed 45-65, flow 18-22% (20% start), top surface speed 80-100 before ironing; denser infill (20-25%) is [hipotese].

scenarios.name: half of a Cut part glued face to face (object scope): shells and walls are raised and the elephant foot widened, but all three rules are hypotheses so the object gets suggestions only
scenarios.review: OK 15.5 (L579-581) and 8.5 (L332): 3-4 walls, 5 top/bottom layers and elephant foot 0.18-0.25 are [hipotese]; object scope, suggestions only.

scenarios.name: plain PLA Basic part on the A1 with explicit settings and every part fact known and unremarkable: nothing is applied, suggested or reported
scenarios.review: OK: every guard is false; nothing changes.

scenarios.name: same part with no facts at all except the printer: unknown conditions skip every rule, nothing changes
scenarios.review: OK: unknown conditions skip every rule.

sequences.description: X2D, PLA Silk: round 0 slows the outer wall to 60 mm/s for gloss; round 1 the G-code shows the Bowden nozzle above 200 mm/s and 1000 mm/s2 on extrusion. The caps are written on the Bowden elements only (the main nozzle keeps 300 mm/s and the preset acceleration) and the 60 mm/s survives (bound-on-top).

Support off, tree(auto), unsupported overhang in the mesh: round 1 sees no support lines and turns support on (critical-only stays off); round 2 still no lines and disables Remove small overhangs; round 3 the lines exist and the ladder is quiet. Painted support keeps the ladder idle.
The 3MF already carries painted support: the ladder does not move even with an unsupported overhang and no support lines.
Thin text on a project already in Arachne: step 1 (wall_generator arachne) is a no-op and is skipped, so the first measured round already writes the 75% / 15% limits.

Part with a long bridge, A1, support off. Round 0 changes nothing (post-slice ladder); round 1 the slice has 0 support lines and the mesh 420 mm2 of unsupported overhang: enable_support 1; round 2 support and interface lines exist, the ladder is quiet and stays at level 1, but the interface-layers choice (relato) raises Top interface layers to 3 (a change, so not done); round 3 nothing changes: done.
sequences.review: DATA as the single-round bridge case (the overhang trigger cannot tell a bridge from a slope). Mechanics OK: step 1, then quiet; the interface-layers choice (6.2 L210) changes a key in round 2, so done only comes in round 3.

sequences.description: Long bridge, A1, support off, and the slicer keeps emitting 0 support lines: round 1 enable_support, round 2 support_remove_small_overhang 0, round 3 the ladder is exhausted (done stays false, the caller must report the exhausted text).
sequences.review: OK ladder mechanics: two steps, then exhausted (done stays false, stalled). DATA: step 2 (Remove small overhangs off) is the data author's guess, not guide text (L215 only names the option).

sequences.description: Same bridge but the project already has Remove small overhangs off: step 2 is a no-op, so after enable_support the next round exhausts the ladder at once (no slice round is spent on the no-op).
sequences.review: OK engine rule (c): a no-op step is skipped and the ladder is exhausted without spending a slice.

sequences.description: Functional bracket with 45-degree overhangs (above the 30-degree threshold): the mesh has no unsupported overhang and the slice has no support, so the support ladder never fires and the sequence is done after the first measured round (support only where needed).
sequences.review: OK 6.1 (L193) and 6.3 (L215): support only where needed; 45 degrees is above the 30-degree threshold (if it is measured from the horizontal, which the guide does not say), so the ladder never fires. The functional-strength suggestions stay suggestions.

sequences.description: Tree support already on with 2 interface layers; the first slice has support lines but no interface: round 1 raises Top interface layers to 3; round 2 the interface exists and the sequence is done.
sequences.review: OK 6.2 (L210) and 6.5 (L233): 3 interface layers is the guide's first option.

sequences.description: Support without interface that no step cures: round 1 interface layers 3, round 2 interface layers 4, round 3 the ladder is exhausted and done stays false.
sequences.review: OK 6.2 (L210): 3 then 4 layers, then the exhausted text (update Studio, 6.5 L233).

sequences.description: Keychain with 0.5 mm lettering on the A1: round 1 six thin features are missing in the G-code, wall_generator arachne; round 2 three still missing, Minimum wall width 75% and Minimum feature size 15%; round 3 none missing: done.
Lettering that never prints: arachne, then the 75% and 15% limits, then exhausted (the guide's remedy is geometric: thicken the stroke to 0.85 to 1.00 mm).
sequences.review: OK: exhausted text is geometric (thicken the stroke to 0.85-1.00 mm, L288, L515).

sequences.description: X2D, PLA Basic, the user had Z-hop off, Auto infill retraction and Grid. Round 0 (predictive, before any slice) switches Z-hop 0.4 on; round 1 the slice has 12 unprotected travels crossing printed lines: ladder step 1, Reduce infill retraction Disabled; round 2 still 5: step 2, Gyroid; round 3 none: nothing changes, done.
sequences.review: OK 5.4 (L162-168): the guide's order of cost is Z-hop on first (round 0, predictive; Z-hop only exists with a retraction, 5.1 L131), then Reduce infill retraction Disabled [relato] (round 1), then a non-crossing infill pattern [relato] (round 2), then slice and READ the G-code (every round). done only comes in round 3, when the measured count is 0 and nothing changes. DATA: round 0 and the ladder steps say nothing about 'Floating vertical shell', the origin of most crossings in the real X2D sample; whether a step reaches it is only known by measuring. The Gyroid step is a hypothesis (weak:true) and the report must say so.

sequences.description: A1, the user had Z-hop off, Grid. Round 0 switches Z-hop 0.4 on; round 1 12 crossing travels: Disabled; round 2 still 5: Gyroid; round 3 still 5 and no step is left: the ladder is exhausted (done stays false, the caller must report the exhausted text with the residual count); round 4 the same, nothing moves.
sequences.review: OK ladder mechanics and honesty (5.4 L160 cause b: turning the option off does not fix everything): two steps, then exhausted with done false and stalled. The caller must report the exhausted text with the residual crossing count, its split by origin and the untried mitigations (brim, support walls, slower infill, bed +5 C, smaller retraction_minimum_travel, Avoid crossing wall), and never say ready. Replaces the earlier pinned case in which the same persisting count produced done: true.

sequences.description: X2D, Auto and Grid. Round 1 the G-code scan failed and the crossing count is missing: the ladder trigger is unknown, no step is taken, done stays false and the round is stalled (never 'clean'); round 2 the scan is back with 4 crossings: step 1; round 3 none: done.
sequences.review: OK: with the crossing count missing the trigger is unknown, the level never moves and the round is stalled with done false; the next round, with the fact back, resumes at step 1. Same rule as seq-unknown-trigger-blocks-done, applied to the travel ladder.

sequences.description: X2D, Auto and Grid, with gcode.unprotected_travel_crossing_count declared unavailable (the analyzer cannot produce it): the ladder trigger is unknown but blind, no step is ever taken and done does NOT stay false; the engine returns the fact in blind_facts and the report must list travel protection as something the engine cannot see.
sequences.review: DATA/ENGINE: a fact in options.unavailable never blocks done, so the sequence is done: true although travel protection was NOT checked. The code port must return the blind fact (blind_facts) and the report must put 'travel collisions: not verified' among what the engine cannot see; done is not ready.

sequences.description: X2D whose project already has Reduce infill retraction Disabled (and Grid): round 1 12 crossing travels: step 1 is a no-op and is skipped, step 2 (Gyroid) is taken in the same round (no slice is spent on the no-op); round 2 none: done.
sequences.review: OK engine rule (c): the project already has Disabled (5.5 L177), so step 1 is skipped (advanced.skipped_noop 1) and Gyroid is taken in the same round; no slice is spent on a no-op.

sequences.description: X2D whose project already has Disabled and Gyroid: both ladder steps are no-ops, so round 1 with 12 crossing travels exhausts the ladder at once without changing anything (done false: the settings cannot fix what the G-code shows).
sequences.review: OK engine rule (c): both steps are no-ops, so the ladder is exhausted at once and nothing changes (5.4 L160: Disabled does not fix everything). done stays false; the report carries the residual count and the untried mitigations.

sequences.description: X2D, PLA Basic, Auto infill retraction and a user-chosen Honeycomb (the guide says only Grid and Triangles cross lines, 5.6 L183): round 1 12 crossing travels: step 1, Disabled; round 2 still 5: step 2 is skipped by its guard (the pattern does not cross), so the ladder is exhausted at once and the pattern stays Honeycomb (never overwritten by Gyroid); round 3 the same, done stays false.
sequences.review: OK 5.6 (L183): only Grid and Triangles cross lines in the same layer and 'Rectilinear tambem evita o cruzamento' (L656), so a Honeycomb project is not changed to Gyroid; the step guard (sparse_infill_pattern in grid/triangles) is false, step 2 is skipped and, being the last, the ladder is exhausted: done false, the report carries the residual count by origin and says the pattern was left alone. DATA: the guide does not order the non-crossing alternatives (L656), so none is tried.

sequences.description: A1, Bambu PETG Basic (stickiness High) already tuned by the user, Auto infill retraction and Grid: round 1 12 crossing travels: step 1 is skipped by its guard (Auto already retracts in infill for High, 5.5 L176) and step 2, Gyroid, is taken in the same round (skipped_noop 1); the skipped step is never written, so reduce_infill_retraction_mode stays Auto; round 2 none: done.
sequences.review: OK 5.5 (L176-179): for stickiness High Auto already retracts in infill, so Disabled is skipped by its guard (advanced.skipped_noop 1) and never written (the settings delta has no reduce_infill_retraction_mode); Gyroid (5.6 L183, hipotese, weak) is the only step taken. DATA: Bambu PETG Basic with 'Floating vertical shell' as the origin of most crossings would still be exhausted, as in the sample; the sequence only pins the mechanics.

sequences.description: Generic (third-party, stickiness None) PETG on the A1 with Grid: round 0 the creators' PETG rule switches the infill to Gyroid before any slice; round 1 12 crossing travels: step 1, Disabled; round 2 still 5: step 2 (Gyroid) is already in effect, so the ladder is exhausted at once and no slice round is spent on an empty step (before the fix the level moved 1 to 2 with zero changes and the exhaustion only came a round later).
sequences.review: OK engine rule (c) extended: a value written by a sticky definite in an earlier round counts as already in effect (5.6 L183, 9.3 L370 creators' PETG table: Gyroid). The empty level move of the earlier engine is gone; the exhaustion arrives in the first round that cannot change anything.

sequences.description: X2D, PLA Basic: round 1 the G-code shows the Bowden nozzle at 250 mm/s and 4000 mm/s2 on extrusion, the caps are written on the Bowden elements; round 2 it measures 200 and 1000 and the caps stay (sticky) with nothing more to change: done.
sequences.review: OK L405, L451: the caps are sticky once written (definite actions re-resolve against the base) and the sequence is done when the re-measurement is within the limit.

sequences.description: Bridge, A1: round 1 the G-code scan failed and gcode.support_line_count is missing: the ladder trigger is unknown, nothing moves, done stays false and the round is stalled; round 2 the scan is back (0 lines): step 1.
sequences.review: OK: an unknown trigger never moves a ladder and never counts as clean; done stays false and the round is stalled until the facts come back.

sequences.description: Organic miniature on the A1, support off, tiny part: round 0 slows the first layer; round 1 no support lines, enable_support; round 2 lines but no interface: interface layers 3 and the organic tree style with one support wall; round 3 the interface exists, nothing changes: done.
sequences.review: OK mechanics (support off, then on, then interface, then clean) and OK 10.4 (L399), 6.3 (L215), 6.2 (L210). DATA: brim and +5 C for tiny parts (L399) are not modelled.

sequences.description: ABS on the X2D with Top Z 0.30 (above the 0.24 to 0.26 range): round 0 (pre-slice) only does the ABS basics; round 1 the slice shows support lines and the post-slice Top Z/Bottom Z choices fire for the first time; round 2 nothing changes: done.
sequences.review: OK phase behaviour: post-slice choices fire in the first round whose facts make them true (6.2 L203 ABS 0.24-0.26) and are then sticky.

sequences.description: Large flat ABS plate on the X2D: round 0 applies the brim and the cooling delay from part facts only (predictive); round 1 the slice is clean and the engine says done, although nothing in the slice measures warping.
sequences.review: DATA: brim and cooling delay come from part facts only (9.4 L377); after a clean slice the engine says done although nothing in the slice measures warping. The report must say 'predicted, not verified by slicing'. Round 1 carries gcode.first_layer_brim_present / first_layer_contact_share, which no action consumes (no brim ladder exists).

sequences.description: Organic miniature on the A1 with tree support: the slice shows 24 unprotected travels inside the support island (the guide's own example, 5.4 cause b). No action moves any key for that counter, and the one that touches the support wall is explicitly blocked by it, so the engine changes nothing and reports done in round 2 while the measured problem is still there.
sequences.review: DATA (central requirement): the support-island example of 5.4 (L160: 24 unprotected travels) is not handled: the rule is a no_action (no measurable trigger) and tune.support.fragile-tree-wall is blocked by the counter, so the engine changes nothing and reports done with the problem still measured. Pinned as today's behaviour, not as the desired one. The invented facts have gcode.unprotected_travel_crossing_count = 0 (the 24 island travels cross nothing printed), so the travel ladder (ENG) stays idle; with crossings it would walk to exhaustion without helping (5.4 cause b), see seq-travel-ladder-exhausted.

sequences.description: X2D: round 1 the Bowden nozzle runs at 250 mm/s and the caps are written; round 2 the G-code STILL shows 250 mm/s (a speed the 11 capped keys do not control, for example a per-object override) and nothing else is left to change: the engine says done although the official limit is still exceeded (the cap is a definite action, not a ladder, so there is no exhausted state to report).
sequences.review: DATA/ENGINE: the official 200 mm/s limit (L49, L405, L451) is still exceeded after the caps, yet the engine says done: the cap is a definite action, not a ladder, so there is no exhausted state to report. Pinned as today's behaviour, not as the desired one.
